{{Short description|Collective name for 2 closely-related conjectures in probability theory}}
'''Ibragimov–Iosifescu conjecture for φ-mixing sequences''' in [[probability theory]] is the collective name for 2 closely related conjectures by Ildar Ibragimov<ref>I.A. Ibragimov and [[Yuri Linnik|Yu.V. Linnik]], Independent and Stationary Sequences of Random Variables, [[:nl:Noordhoff Uitgevers|Wolters-Noordhoff]], [[Groningen]], 1971, p. 393, problem 3.</ref> and [[:ro:Marius Iosifescu]].<ref>M. Iosifescu, Limit theorems for ϕ-mixing sequences, a survey. In: Proceedings of the Fifth Conference on Probability Theory, [[Brașov]], 1974, pp. 51-57. [[:ro:Editura Academiei Române|Publishing House of the Romanian Academy]], [[Bucharest]], 1977.</ref>

== Conjecture ==
Let <math>(X_n,n\in\Bbb N)</math> be a strictly stationary <math>\phi</math>-mixing sequence, for which <math>\mathbb E(X_0^2)<\infty</math> and <math>\operatorname{Var}(S_n)\to +\infty</math>. Then <math>S_n:=\sum_{j=1}^nX_j</math> is asymptotically normally distributed.

<math>\phi</math>
-mixing coefficients are defined as
<math>\phi_X(n):=\sup(|\mu(B\mid A)-\mu(B)|, A\in\mathcal F^m, B\in \mathcal F_{m+n},m\in\Bbb N )</math>,
where <math>\mathcal F^m</math> and <math>\mathcal F_{m+n}</math> are the <math>\sigma</math>-algebras generated by the <math>X_j, j\leqslant m</math> (respectively <math>j\geqslant m+n</math>), and <math>\phi</math>-mixing means that <math>\phi_X(n)\to 0</math>.

Reformulated:

Suppose <math>X:=(X_k, k \in {\mathbf Z})</math> is a strictly stationary sequence of random variables such that
<math>EX_0 = 0, \ EX_0^2 < \infty</math> and <math>ES_n^2 \to \infty</math> as <math>n \to \infty</math> (that is, such that it has finite second moments and <math>\operatorname{Var}(X_1 + \ldots + X_n) \to \infty</math> as <math>n \to \infty</math>).

Per Ibragimov, under these assumptions, if also <math>X</math> is <math>\phi</math>-mixing, then a central limit theorem holds. Per a closely related conjecture by Iosifescu, under the same hypothesis, a weak invariance principle holds. Both conjectures together formulated in similar terms:

Let <math>\{X_n\}_n</math> be a strictly stationary, centered, <math>\phi</math>-mixing sequence of random variables such that <math>EX^2_1 < \infty</math> and <math>\sigma^2_n \to \infty</math>. Then per Ibragimov <math>S_n / \sigma_n \overset{W}{\to} N(0, 1)</math>, and per Iosifescu <math>S_{[n1]} / \sigma_n \overset{W}{\to} W</math>. Also, a related conjecture by [[Magda Peligrad]] states that under the same conditions and with <math>\phi_1 < 1</math>, <math>\overset{\sim}{W}_n \overset{W}{\to} W</math>.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Peligrad |first=Magda |date=August 1990 |title=On Ibragimov–Iosifescu conjecture for φ-mixing sequences |url= |journal=Stochastic Processes and Their Applications |volume=35 |issue=2 |pages=293–308 |doi=10.1016/0304-4149(90)90008-G |access-date=|doi-access= }}
</ref>

== Relation to other mixing conditions ==
The conjecture occupies an important position in the theory of dependent stochastic processes because φ-mixing is one of the strongest classical mixing conditions. A large number of central limit theorems are known for stationary processes satisfying stronger assumptions on dependence, while the precise behaviour of φ-mixing sequences under only finite-variance assumptions remained less well understood.

A sequence is φ-mixing if future events become asymptotically independent of past events in a uniform sense. The φ-mixing condition is stronger than the more widely studied α-mixing (strong mixing) condition. Consequently, many probabilists expected that a central limit theorem should hold under relatively weak moment assumptions for φ-mixing sequences.

The conjecture is therefore closely connected with the broader question of determining which dependence assumptions are sufficient to guarantee asymptotic normality of partial sums.

== Status ==
In September 2026, a candidate counterexample to the conjecture was announced by Tom Adamczewski in a public GitHub repository.<ref name="phi-mixing-clt">{{cite web
 |title=Ibragimov–Iosifescu conjecture for φ-mixing sequences
 |url=https://github.com/tadamcz/phi-mixing-clt
 |website=GitHub
 |access-date=15 September 2026
}}</ref> The counterexample was generated by [[GPT-6 Astra]] and formalised in the [[Lean (proof assistant)]]. If correct, the construction disproves Ibragimov's central limit theorem conjecture and consequently disproves Iosifescu's stronger weak invariance principle conjecture.<ref name="phi-mixing-clt" /> This result remains unaudited by the mathematical community and presents the construction as a candidate disproof pending independent verification.<ref name="phi-mixing-clt" />
